hub/meta.name: LFTG Performance Index
hub/meta.combinedNote: 347-225, +90.5u, 2021–26 at the opener (v3.4 spreads 276-181 + unders 5+ 71-44). Untested 2017–19 seasons vs the close: 144-138 (51.1%).

method.h: What the LFTG Performance Index is
method.p: Each team gets opponent-adjusted offense and defense ratings for success rate, explosiveness, rushing and passing efficiency, line yards, stuff rate and short-yardage success, updated after every game, plus a margin-of-victory rating, Elo and (new in v3.1) a market rating: a running team rating built from past closing point spreads, so the index learns from what the betting market already knew before each game. v3.1 also adds a travel factor and updates ratings faster during the season, and each new season starts from 90% of the previous season's margin rating. Team talent sets the rest of the preseason starting point and fades as games are played. Weights come from a ridge regression refit every Sunday. In testing, v3.1 cut prediction error in every season from 2017 to 2026 and was the first version above .500 against the closing line in seasons never used to build it (2017–19). Teams are ranked by rating; the Ratings tab also shows a résumé (strength-of-record) rank.

Rosters turn over much faster now. Incoming transfers per FBS team went from about 6 in 2021 to 22 in 2026, and returning offensive production fell from about 61% (2015–19 average) to about 40% (2025–26). In November 2026 we re-tested the index on the portal era alone: seasons 2022–26, each predicted by a model fit only on earlier seasons. Three changes helped and are now in v3.4: (1) the weights are refit with recent seasons counting more (a season's weight halves every three years); (2) a recency-weighted least-squares team rating, where the last few games count most, joins the ratings; (3) in Weeks 1–6, returning production counts less than it did before 2021. What didn't help: transfer-portal talent, incoming transfer QBs, losing a starting QB, first-year head coaches and four-year recruiting added nothing beyond talent, returning production and early results. Cutting last season's carry-over or changing the market rating didn't help either. In the 2022–26 test v3.4 lowered average error (15.35 to 15.31 points), its edges were more predictive against both the opener and the close, and its picks went 231-145 (61.4%) at the opener vs 219-161 for v3.1 (215-171 vs 212-172 against the close). It had smaller misses in 4 of 5 seasons (2025 was slightly worse). The gain is modest and mostly in Group of Five games, so v3.1 is still logged alongside it.

Every hour the index re-checks every game on the latest lines. A pick is a Best Bet only if it clears the bar at the opening line: in 2021–26, 58% of qualifying picks saw the market move toward the index before kickoff, and those won 63%. Picks that only qualify after the line moves off the opener went 50.0% (105-105), so they are shown as Leans with an "after line move" tag. Lean = edge 3–4 (spreads) or 3–5 (unders), or an after-line-move pick; not a bet.

Power-conference games (SEC, Big Ten, Big 12, ACC, Notre Dame and other independents): edge of 4+ against the best available line. G5-only games, including the rebuilt Pac-12: edge of 4–6 only; bigger G5 edges are treated as model error. (v3.1 edges are smaller because the index now includes the market's own view, so the bar moved from 5 to 4. Full v3.4 backtest, each 2021–26 season predicted only from earlier seasons: 276-181, 60.4% at the opener.) No best bets in Weeks 1–3 or bowls. Big moves: if the line moves 3+ points against a pick after it opens, the pick drops to a Lean (picks the market moved away from went 49.6%).

Unders only, model 5+ points below the opening total (4–5 point edges went 53.7%, 5+ went 71-44, 61.7%). Since Nov 21, 2026 an under is passed if the total rises 1 point or more after it opens (was 3): in 2021–26, 5+ unders whose total then rose 1+ went 11-13, while the rest went 60-31 (65.9%) at the opener and 53-38 at the closing number. Expect about one or two totals a week, not more. The index lowers its total by about a point for late-season games (Week 10 on) in outdoor stadiums at 39°N or farther north. Overs at the same edge went 47%, so they are never bet. The index still doesn't see the forecast: check wind and rain before betting a total.

Lines refresh every hour, 9 AM to 11 PM ET, Monday–Saturday, until each game kicks off. Every Sunday before 9 AM the season data is refreshed, the index is refit, power ratings are republished and next week's games are projected, with early best bets wherever openers are posted.

Bet early and shop the number. The index's edge is mostly about where the line is going: in 2021–26, when a pick qualified at the opener, the market moved toward the index 58% of the time. Waiting usually means a worse number. Buying onto or off 3 is worth up to about −125. Check QB news before every bet: the market already prices known QB changes.
CollegeFootballData.com: games, lines, play-by-play efficiency, Elo, talent and returning production, 2014–present. Every backtest number uses only information available before kickoff.

method.h: Outside ratings: SP+, FPI and SRS (v3.5)
method.p: Since Nov 21, each game's projected margin and each team's power rating blend 85% of the model with 15% of a consensus of three public ratings: Bill Connelly's SP+, ESPN's FPI and the Simple Rating System (SRS), refreshed daily from CollegeFootballData (CFBD's Elo was already a model input). Best bets, leans, upset alerts and parlays all use the blended number, and player props use it for game script (15% of the projected spread and total, 85% the market). Why 15%: no week-by-week archive of SP+ or FPI exists to backtest, so the weight was set by how well each blend matched this week's betting lines; the model alone matched within 2.0 points a game, the consensus alone 2.9, and blends of 10–20% did best. The model's own margin is still logged for every game so the blend can be graded against it through the bowls. The backtest record shown here is for the model without the outside ratings.

Named FBS rivalries (214 pairs, from trophy games like the Iron Bowl and Paul Bunyan's Axe to the Egg Bowl and The Game) are tagged on the board. In 2014–26, home teams in those games finished 1.2 points worse than the closing spread (1,492 games; 1.4 in 2014–19, 1.0 in 2021–26), while home teams in other games matched it. So the index takes 1.0 point of home field off in rivalry games. The "throw out the records" idea didn't hold up: rivalry underdogs covered 50.0% against the close and 47.9% against the opener, and rivalry totals went 51.8% under, no different from other games.

Since Nov 25: if a team's usual starting QB (its starter last game) is listed Out, Doubtful, Questionable or a game-time decision, that game can't be a Best Bet; it drops to Lean with a "check news" note until the starter is confirmed. The index has no QB input, so a big edge in these games is often just the QB news the market has already priced. Already-logged bets stay in the tracker.
